headline: A0 is 4-of-6 and A6 is 3-of-4 on the DEPLOYED body. The crystal target reaches DerivedAgreed under the stage1 (T2d) trustc and its lineage digest is re-pinned, but it DOES NOT FLIP: two independent fail-closed gates refuse it (the -O lifetime-marker gate, markers_exact=false; and the wave-TR thin-reborrow provenance lane). 1_consumer_perturbation_on_the_deployed_.control: -Ztrust-sat-perturb=switch-map (the compiler's own burn-in control: rotate the switch value->target map one position AFTER the canonical sort)
1_consumer_perturbation_on_the_deployed_.target_body_result: level::Level::is_zero goes agreed -> MISMATCH, and the comparator names the corruption exactly: built `b0: switch(disc(isize,deref(a1)))[0->b1,1->b2,2->b3,3->b10,4->b13,else->b14]` vs derived `...[0->b1,1->b2,2->b9,3->b12,4->b13,else->b14]`. The A0 `agreed` verdict is therefore NOT vacuous.
1_consumer_perturbation_on_the_deployed_.crate_result: 185 -> 175 flip events. 22 bodies had the perturbation APPLIED (applications>0); 11 of those flipped unperturbed; 10 of the 11 stop flipping. The 11th (`mode::CleanMode::has_cubical_layer`) still flips and that is CORRECT, not a hole: its switch is `[ 2: bb1  3: bb2 ]` where bb1 and bb2 are both `const bool true; br bb4`, so rotating the target list is the identity. Every lost flip is exactly a body the perturbation reached.
1_consumer_perturbation_on_the_deployed_.scope_note: -Ztrust-sat-perturb perturbs the CONSUMER (the shim), not the artifact, so the lineage digests are unchanged by it (verified: has_cubical_layer's event digest is identical in both builds, sha256:a7acae485be7faba9d538c393e7f5456b2fd3155f76d9f5a5f2c4bd68c40a185). It tests the comparator, not the attestation.

2_artifact_perturbation_on_the_digest.fixture: scratchpad/a6/probe.rs — two bodies, `wide` (subject) and `untouched` (control); the perturbation is one literal in `wide` (7 -> 8) selected by --cfg perturb; both compilations otherwise byte-identical argv
2_artifact_perturbation_on_the_digest.cross_check: the control digest does not appear anywhere in the perturbed build's log, and vice versa; in both builds the event digest equals the coverage row's lineage
2_artifact_perturbation_on_the_digest.conclusion: the flip event's digest is bound to the body's own lowered content: a perturbed artifact cannot produce the pinned digest, and a neighbouring untouched body's digest does not move. A flip that fired regardless of the digest is refuted.

3_source_level_fail_closed_NOT_independe.status: read in source and its refusal strings confirmed present in the shipped stage1 driver, but NOT independently triggered — doing so requires tampering inside the compiler process, i.e. a modified trustc, which needs a compiler rebuild this job did not perform.

why_the_target_body_does_not_flip.attempted_and_blocked: the same isolation directly on the deployed crate (`cargo build --release` with -Copt-level=0 appended to the clean_kernel unit only) could not be run: mid-session another agent's sibling-crate version bump left $USER_HOME inconsistent with its path dependencies, so `--locked` refused, and rewriting a shared lockfile to work around it was declined.

remaining_to_close_A0_and_A6: T2e (producer): ledger the thin shared reborrow so `thin_reborrow_allows_flip` can admit `Level::is_zero` on its own terms.

Marker fidelity for this body: the derived side emits no `mk`/lifetime-marker line for the `&LevelArc` local, so markers_exact=false at every opt-level > 0. Until it is exact, no release-shaped flip is possible for this body.

Bodyful closure: `Option::as_deref` and `Option::expect` are declaration-only in the artifact, and `<LevelArc as Deref>::deref` is itself DerivedUnsupported (`Call(callee return outside the fragment: Option<&Level>)`). Both are named build items; the seam's refusal to link a bodyless callee must be preserved.
Then re-run this exact probe: A0 needs only the closure + the flip event; A6 needs only the flip event (the digest, its reproduction, and its fail-closed binding are already measured here).
